solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dad called up boor, cheerful, for what’s afflicting orchard?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being called up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A father summons a cheery lout to deal with trouble in the orchard.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple blight is a disease, an aphid infestation, that attacks apple trees in an orchard.

clue.text: Tailless lizard, variable length

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: a varan is a monitor lizard

explanation.surface: A lizard missing its tail, of some indeterminate size.
explanation.walkthrough: VARA is the Spanish and Portuguese yard, a unit whose size differed from region to region.
explanation.definitionFit: The vara is an old Iberian measure of distance whose value varied from place to place.

clue.text: Special girl? Bob may be attached to one in the US

definitions.text: Bob may be attached to one in the US

explanation.surface: A girl asks whether a man called Bob is attached to her in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name; it is the bob in bob skate, an American child's skate with double runners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobskate is a US skate with two parallel blades, so a bob is fixed to one kind of skate.

clue.text: Paper-making machine enveloping craftsman’s head in choking dust

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, at the front
to envelop something is to wrap round it, so one part goes outside the other

blocks.note: a pother is a choking cloud of dust or smoke

explanation.surface: A mill machine swallows a craftsman's head in a cloud of stifling dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A potcher is the engine in paper mills that beats and bleaches the pulp.

clue.text: Love film including shot of snake- worshippers

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a shot that strikes its target

explanation.surface: Someone adores a movie with footage of a cult that venerates serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ophites were an early Gnostic sect who revered the serpent, and ophitic is the adjective for them.

clue.text: Floor lamp? Here goes – it’s made of twisted metal

indicators.note: when something goes it departs, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: a torchère is a tall standard lamp

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a standard lamp, announcing it is made of twisted wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here goes' reads as a cheerful 'let's try'; it actually tells you to remove HERE from TORCHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a Celtic neck ring formed from strands of gold or bronze twisted together.

clue.text: Managing with old mirror that’s skew

blocks.note: stone is an obsolete word for a looking-glass, as in King Lear

explanation.surface: Getting by with an antique mirror that hangs crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skew' looks like an adjective for the mirror; it is a noun, a sloping stone on top of a gable.
explanation.definitionFit: A skew is the sloping coping at the top of a gable wall, a kind of capping block.

clue.text: Tackle degree lacking in difficulty?

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: the quality of being hard to do

explanation.surface: Does facing a problem take some degree of difficulty?
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is the gear for a horse or a load, which is what a harness is.

clue.text: Further attempt to clear up that’s over

blocks.note: red is a variant of redd, to tidy or clear up

explanation.surface: Another go at tidying up what has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Redd, also spelt red, is a Scots and dialect verb for putting a room in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A redo is a second go at something, doing it over again.

clue.text: Swelling having blood round it

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

explanation.surface: A lump with blood all around it, like an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, a visible lump on the neck.

clue.text: Kinsman not opening case (common in Helsinki?)

indicators.note: without its opening, the word loses the letter it starts with

explanation.surface: A relative declines to open a legal case, perhaps one heard in Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a suitcase or lawsuit; it is a grammatical case, and Finnish nouns use this one constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The elative is a grammatical case meaning 'out of', standard in Finnish.

clue.text: Legatee confused about obfuscation in cable?

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order
about means placed round the other piece

explanation.surface: An heir is baffled by unclear wording in a telegram about a bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: Telemessage was the name for the service that replaced the telegram, which was also called a cable.

clue.text: Chinese house (in Sydney?) creating a stink beside magnolia cham removed

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so those named letters are dropped

blocks.note: the champak or champaka is an Indian tree of the magnolia family

explanation.surface: An Australian Chinese home smells next to a magnolia tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is the game of housey-housey; pakapoo is a Chinese lottery played in Australia, hence 'in Sydney'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pakapoo is a Chinese form of lottery, a numbers game like house or bingo, played in Australia.

clue.text: Spiny spot on cactus, one with end of prickle in part

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
in means placed inside the other piece

explanation.surface: A prickly patch on a cactus plays its part.
explanation.definitionFit: An areole is the small cushion on a cactus from which its spines grow.

clue.text: Nippy sailing vessel turned up with senior naval officer on board

indicators.note: turned round means read the other way
aboard means carried inside the vessel, so that piece goes within

explanation.surface: A speedy boat arrived carrying a high-ranking naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'arrived', but 'turned' acts on the word up itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A prau is a fast Malay sailing boat, famous for its speed.

clue.text: Servile rustic to call up beforehand?

explanation.surface: Should one phone a farmhand ahead of time?
explanation.walkthrough: Wordplay reads back to front: PRE (beforehand) comes first, then DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Predial means attached to the land, as a serf or farm labourer bound to an estate.

clue.text: Piece of Venetian glass showing Latin citation, translated

indicators.note: translating something puts it into a new form, so these letters change their arrangement

explanation.surface: A glass ornament from Venice bears an inscription in Latin, rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole word Latin wants to be fodder; only its abbreviation L is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Latticino is Venetian glass worked with threads of opaque white, or an article made of it.

clue.text: Earl opening activity to raise money?

explanation.surface: A nobleman opens a charity fundraiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundraising event is an organised occasion held for charity.

clue.text: Ne’er-do-well that is confined to jug having gone after Virginia

indicators.note: confined means shut inside something

explanation.surface: A wastrel is locked up in jail after chasing a girl called Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' suggests prison; here it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaurien is a French-derived word for a worthless rogue or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Disturbs fitness exercises

indicators.note: exercising works something over, putting these letters through moves into a new order

explanation.surface: Workouts at the gym prove upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercises' looks like a noun completing the phrase; it is a verb working on the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests that overrun a place trouble and plague it.

clue.text: Foreign highness sets out in October as before

indicators.note: out means disordered, so those letters are rearranged
in means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: October was formerly a strong ale brewed in that month

explanation.surface: A foreign royal departs in October, as in previous years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' looks like 'as last year'; it marks October as an archaic word for ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Altesse is French for highness, a royal title of address.

clue.text: Unattractive expression one pulled?

indicators.note: something pulled is withdrawn, so that piece comes out

explanation.surface: Is this the ugly face somebody pulled?
explanation.walkthrough: 'One pulled' reads as a face someone made; ACE leaves GRIMACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim can mean forbidding or unpleasant to look at, the opposite of attractive.

clue.text: Waist and leg been adjusted, volume taken in? Tailored feature shrinking from end to end (13, two words)

definitions.text: Tailored feature shrinking from end to end

indicators.note: taken in means absorbed inside the other letters
adjusted letters are altered and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor alters waist and leg, taking in some volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' sounds like tailoring; it means V goes in among the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A batwing sleeve is wide at the armhole and narrows steadily to the wrist, tapering along its length.

clue.text: Army track uphill after end of fight

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
in a down clue, going uphill means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A military force tracks its way up a hill once the battle ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are soldiers collectively, the body of an army.

clue.text: Dodge, mostly half-hearted, taking king in

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: luke is an old adjective for lukewarm, tepid

explanation.surface: A feeble evasion that lets the monarch in.
explanation.walkthrough: Lurk is Australian slang for a racket or dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurk in Australian English is a scheme or trick for getting an advantage.

clue.text: Singers rarely get beyond these shrines

blocks.note: read as ..., the highest notes most voices reach

explanation.surface: Few choristers venture past these holy places.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TOP E'S: the top E is near the ceiling of most singers' ranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tope is a stupa, a Buddhist mound monument housing relics.

clue.text: Trump’s last East will have to provide taking partner’s last lowish trump

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter
taking means holding something inside

blocks.note: as in doing lunch for guests

explanation.surface: A bridge player sitting East must play a middling trump card.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting misleads: pedro is a card game, and also the five of trumps in it.
explanation.definitionFit: In games such as cinch, the pedro is the five of trumps, a moderately low card that still scores.

clue.text: Here is dry in Rome without sun overhead

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is removed
overhead in a down entry means at the top, so it is the first letter that goes

explanation.surface: Behold the dry, sunless Roman weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' places the sun at the top of a down entry; 'in Rome' serves both the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecco is Italian for 'here is' or 'behold'.

clue.text: Those working in capitals maybe give power to muscle? About right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part is placed round another

blocks.note: the teres is a shoulder muscle

explanation.surface: Do workers in capital cities strengthen their muscles about the right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests cities; it means capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letterers draw or paint lettering, which may well be in capitals.

clue.text: Pawn, raising swag

indicators.note: raising lifts things upwards, which reverses a down entry

explanation.surface: A chess pawn being lifted off with stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is a person used by others, which is what a tool is.

clue.text: Old-fashioned prank eccentric female initially ditched

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter
ditched means thrown away, so that letter goes

explanation.surface: A quaint practical joke in which an odd woman is first dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram signal; here it is a noun meaning FREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Reak is an obsolete word for a trick or prank.

clue.text: I go so coy, endlessly turning whimsical

indicators.note: endlessly means without an ending, so the last letter goes
turning things over changes their order

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to becoming bashful and playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Giocoso is a musical direction meaning playful or merry.

clue.text: Alas, having to miss final piece in such as the Albert Hall?

indicators.note: missing the final piece means the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: Sadly, a concert at a great London hall loses its last item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Albert Hall is a large London concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Odea, plural of odeum, are buildings for musical performance, concert halls in the plural.

clue.text: Knowledgeable jazz fan

blocks.note: in the know, an older form of hip
jazz slang for a fan or musician

explanation.surface: A jazz enthusiast who really knows the music.
explanation.definitionFit: A hepcat is a hip person who follows swing or jazz, in the slang of the 1940s.

clue.text: Runny organ’s bunged by one ultimately?

definitions.text: Runny organ’s bunged by one ultimately?

indicators.note: something runny flows out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the very end, taking the last letter

explanation.surface: A streaming nose is plugged by something, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the thing as well: a streaming nose gets plugged with this.
explanation.definitionFit: A noserag is slang for a handkerchief, the cloth you hold to a dripping nose.

clue.text: It grows on knee of horse, curiously toeless

definitions.text: It grows on knee of horse

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so these letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: Something oddly grows on a horse's knee, which has no toes.
explanation.definitionFit: An osselet is a bony growth on the inside of a horse's knee or fetlock.
